On 9/21/2011 7:21 AM, Peng Yu wrote:
> Hi,
>
> library(ggplot2)
> qplot(class,hwy,data=mpg,geom='boxplot')
>
> I know that boxplot can be plotted in the above way. However, I want to plot
> boxplot where the mean, sd and 25% and 75% quantiles are available, but the
> raw data is not. In other word, suppose I only have the 'tmp' data.frame as
> generated below, I want to plot the boxplot using 'tmp' only (without
> plotting the outliers). But I'm not able to find a way to do it with
> ggplot2. Could anybody kindly let me know how to do it? Thanks!
>
> tmp=do.call(
> rbind
> , lapply(
> with(mpg, split(hwy, class))
> , function(x) {
> data.frame(
> mean=mean(x)
> , sd=sd(x)
> , quantile25=quantile(x,.25)
> , quantile75=quantile(x,.75)
> )
> }
> )
> )
>

It's not really a boxplot, but you can get something close with

tmp$class <- row.names(tmp)

ggplot(tmp, aes(x=class)) +
geom_crossbar(aes(y=mean, ymin=quantile25, ymax=quantile75))

Note that you have to bring the class from just the row names to an
actual column to be able to use it as the x-axis variable.
